| Series types | each series type, with its own keys | [`line`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/line/), [`donut`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/donut/) |
| Axes | the keys of an axis, with the scales each holds for | [`scale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/), [`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/) |
| Setup | the third argument of `chart()`: `types`, `features`, `messages`, `animate` | [`types`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/types/), [`features`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/features/) |
| Features | each feature of `@dzgraph/dom`, and the options that need it | [`zoom`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/zoom/), [`timeAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/time-axis/) |

An axis option is given in `xAxis` or `yAxis`, one axis or a list of them; a series option in each entry of `series`.

## Reading a facts table

This is the table of [`aspectRatio`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/aspect-ratio/):

Type: `number`. Default: `16 / 9`.

- **Type**: as the types write it.
- **Default**, or **Required** when the option has none.
- **Needs**: the feature to give `chart()` in `features`. Without it the option is reported (`missing-module`) and the
  chart draws without it.
- **Live update**: how a new value reaches a chart already drawn.
- **Angular**: how `<dz-chart>` takes it.
- **Declared in**: the line of the sources, on GitHub.

A script reads these facts from the sources, and the site's tests check them: that each page shows its own, that every
option has a page, and that each « Needs » is the feature the chart really asks for.

## Updating options

`update()` takes any top-level field of the options:

- a field given replaces the previous one whole: no deep merge to guess about;
- a field given as `undefined` goes back to its default;
- a field left out is kept;
- `series` is matched by `id`: a series that keeps its id keeps the user's state on it and is animated from where it
  was.

What the user did — a zoom, a hidden series, a selection — is the view, and new options never overwrite it.
`setData()` replaces one series' values, the cheapest way to show new numbers; the next `update()` that gives that
series' data wins over it. The setup (`types`, `features`, `messages`, `animate`) is read once, when the chart is made;
in Angular a new value of those inputs draws a new chart.

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(document.getElementById('load')!, { title: { text: 'Load (made up)' }, series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'load', data: [12, 15, 11] }] }, { types: [line] });

c.update({ legend: false });
c.update({ title: undefined });
c.setData('load', [12, 15, 11, 18]);
```

## Options the chart cannot read

A bad option never throws. A key the chart does not know is reported `unknown-option`, a value it cannot read
`invalid-option`, an option without its feature `missing-module`, each with its path (`yAxis[0].min`); the chart draws
what it can. The problems are in `c.problems` and the `problems` event, and never carry your data.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/animation/ -->

# animation

Animating the chart's appearing and its updates.

Type: `boolean`. Default: `true`.

## What it does

When the chart appears (400 ms), lines and areas are revealed from the start of the x axis, columns and bars
grow from their baseline, markers fade in. When it is updated (250 ms) — new options, new data, a series hidden from
the legend — what stays moves from where it was, what comes grows from the baseline, what goes fades out. A resize is
never animated.

`false` turns all of it off: the chart shows its end state at once. So does the reader's system setting for reduced
motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`), whatever this option says. To drive the animations yourself (GSAP, for
instance), give `chart()` an [`animate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/animate/) function.

A value other than a boolean is reported (`invalid-option` at `animation`).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('animation')!,
  {
    animation: false,
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'crates', name: 'Crates', data: [12, 19, 15, 22, 17] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## See also

- [`animate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/animate/): animations driven by the app.
- [Interactions](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/interactions/): animation with the other interactions.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/aspect-ratio/ -->

# aspectRatio

Width ÷ height, for an element without a height of its own.

Type: `number`. Default: `16 / 9`.

## What it does

The chart takes its element's size and follows it. Its height comes from the element — a CSS height, a grid or
flex cell — never from its content, so the chart does not jump when its data changes. When the element has no height
of its own, the chart takes its width and this ratio: `2` is twice as wide as tall.

A value that is not a positive finite number is reported (`invalid-option` at `aspectRatio`) and the default is used.

## Example

```ts
import { area } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('aspect-ratio')!,
  {
    aspectRatio: 3,
    series: [{ type: 'area', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain (mm)', data: [12, 18, 9, 22, 30, 14, 8] }],
  },
  { types: [area] },
);
```

## See also

- [TypeScript](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/getting-started/typescript/): the element's size.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/crosshair/ -->

# crosshair

Lines through the pointer, with its values on the axes.

Type: `boolean | { readonly horizontal?: boolean }`. Default: `false`. Needs the `crosshair` feature.

## What it does

`true` draws a dashed vertical line that follows the pointer exactly, not snapped to the points, and a tag at its foot
with the x value there, written as the tooltip writes it. `{ horizontal: true }` adds a horizontal line and a tag on
each value axis. With the keyboard the lines go through the focused point. The lines stay in the measure and selection
modes, to help aim. Not on a pie, a donut or a gauge.

Without the `crosshair` feature the option is reported (`missing-module`) and nothing is drawn.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, crosshair } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('tide')!,
  {
    crosshair: { horizontal: true },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'tide', name: 'Tide (m)', data: [1.2, 3.8, 5.1, 2.4, 0.9, 3.6] }],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [crosshair] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the crosshair with the other ways to read a chart.
- [`crosshair`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/crosshair/), the feature.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/data-table/ -->

# dataTable

The table of the chart's numbers: for screen readers, or shown under the chart.

Type: `boolean | { readonly show?: boolean; readonly rows?: 'visible' | 'all' }`. Default: `false`.

## What it does

Every chart has a data table: a row per x, a column per visible series, the same numbers as the chart. By default
it is hidden from sight and read by screen readers, after the chart. `true` shows it under the chart.

The table shown is inside the chart's element, under the chart, and the element's height is the chart's alone. So
give the element no fixed height: the chart takes its `aspectRatio` and the table follows it. With a fixed height,
the table goes past the element and covers what comes next.

An object gives `show` (the same choice) and `rows`. Zoomed, the table shows the visible range and says so in its
caption, with a button to switch to all the data and back; `rows: 'all'` starts it with all the data. The CSV export
follows the same choice. A table holds at most 1 000 rows: past that, its last row says how many were left out (the
CSV gives them all).

Something else than a boolean or an object is `invalid-option` at `dataTable`; another key `unknown-option` at
`dataTable.<key>`; a wrong value `invalid-option` at `dataTable.show` or `dataTable.rows`.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('data-table')!,
  {
    dataTable: { show: true, rows: 'all' },
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug'] },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'plum', name: 'Plum jam', data: [14, 22, 41, 66] }],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## See also

- [Accessibility](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/accessibility/): the data table, with a demo.
- [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/exporting/): the CSV export.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/description/ -->

# description

A sentence for screen readers, after the summary the chart writes.

Type: `string`.

## What it does

The chart is a figure for screen readers, described by a summary it writes itself: its kind, its series and the
range of each, its x axis (« Line chart, 2 series… »). `description` adds the app's sentence after it — what the chart
is for, what to notice. It is not shown on screen. An exported SVG picture carries the same text in its `<desc>`.

A value other than a string is reported (`invalid-option` at `description`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('description')!,
  {
    title: 'Visits (made up)',
    description: 'Visits doubled between January and June.',
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'visits', name: 'Visits', data: [310, 340, 420, 510, 580, 640] }],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## See also

- [`title`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/title/): the name screen readers hear first.
- [Accessibility](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/accessibility/): screen readers, the keyboard, the data table.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/dir/ -->

# dir

The reading direction: left to right, or right to left.

Type: `'ltr' | 'rtl'`. Default: the element’s (`dir` attribute or CSS `direction`).

## What it does

`'rtl'` lays the chart out for right-to-left reading: the title, the legend and the value axis sit on the right,
labels read from the right, the keyboard's arrows follow the reading direction. The x axis itself still runs left to
right, as numbers and dates usually do in those languages, unless [`mirror`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/mirror/) is `true`. Bars grow from the
right.

Without it, the chart takes its element's direction: its `dir` attribute or its CSS `direction`, inherited from the
page. A value other than `'ltr'` or `'rtl'` is reported (`invalid-option` at `dir`) and the element's direction is
used.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('dir')!,
  {
    dir: 'rtl',
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Week 1', 'Week 2', 'Week 3', 'Week 4'] },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'jars', name: 'Jars', data: [18, 24, 21, 30] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`mirror`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/mirror/): the x axis running right to left too.
- [Theming and right to left](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/theming-rtl/): right to left, with an Arabic demo.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/drilldown/ -->

# drilldown

Years, then months, then days, by click, on a time axis.

Type: `'time'`. Needs the `drilldown` feature.

## What it does

`'time'` aggregates a time x axis by year. A click, or Enter on a focused point, shows the months of that year;
another, the days of that month. The level shows its whole period, even past the data's end. A breadcrumb above the
plot goes back to any level, as do Backspace and Alt + ← (→ in right to left); going back restores the level as it
was. The level is part of the view, and the `drill` event gives its path.

It starts from years, whatever the axis's [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/) says. Each series keeps its own
[aggregation function](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/aggregate/) (a sum for columns, a mean for lines).

It needs the [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/drilldown/) feature, which brings
[`aggregation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/): without it, `missing-module` at `drilldown`. Off a time x axis, or with
another value, it is `invalid-option` at `drilldown`. A detail per point, by key or loaded, is a series' own
[`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/drilldown/).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, timeAxis, drilldown } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('drilldown')!,
  {
    drilldown: 'time',
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC' },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain (mm)', data: [['2025-03-04', 12], ['2025-09-18', 30], ['2026-01-05', 9], ['2026-02-21', 14]] }],
  },
  { types: [column], features: [timeAxis, drilldown] },
);

c.on('drill', (e) => console.log(e.path));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/drilldown/): a detail per point.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): aggregation and drilldown.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/exporting/ -->

# exporting

The exports' defaults: the file's name, the pictures' colours, the CSV's separators.

Type: `{ readonly filename?: string; readonly theme?: 'light' | 'dark'; readonly csv?: { readonly locale?: boolean } }`. Needs the `exporting` feature.

## What it does

The chart exports itself through its methods — `exportSvg()`, `exportPng()`, `exportCsv()`, `download()`,
`print()` — and through the reader's [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/). This option gives their defaults:

- `filename`: the downloaded file's name, without its extension. By default the title's letters, digits and hyphens,
  else « chart » in the chart's language.
- `theme`: `'light'` or `'dark'` for the pictures (SVG, PNG). By default they keep the screen's colours: a dark page
  exports dark.
- `csv.locale`: `true` writes semicolons between cells and a decimal comma where the chart's language writes one (as a
  French spreadsheet expects). By default the CSV is universal: commas and dots.

The exports need the [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/exporting/) feature. The option is read without it, but the methods
then do nothing and report `missing-module` at `exporting`. Something else than an object is `invalid-option` at
`exporting`; a wrong key or value `invalid-option` at `exporting.<key>`.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, exporting } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('exporting')!,
  {
    title: 'Crates picked (made up)',
    exporting: { filename: 'crates', theme: 'light', csv: { locale: true } },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'crates', name: 'Crates', data: [12, 19, 15, 22, 17] }],
  },
  { types: [column], features: [exporting] },
);

document.getElementById('save')!.addEventListener('click', () => void c.download('png'));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/): downloads offered to the reader.
- [Export and print](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exporting/): pictures, CSV and printing.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/highlight/ -->

# highlight

Fading the other series while one is pointed at.

Type: `boolean`. Default: `true`.

## What it does

While the pointer is on a column, a bar or a scatter point, the other series fade to 35 %, so the one pointed at
stands out; the tooltip names it. A chart of lines, whose shared tooltip lists every series, fades nothing. `false`
turns the fading off: every series stays as it is.

The highlight is the pointer's only. The fading of a [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/selection/) is another thing and lasts. A value
other than a boolean is reported (`invalid-option` at `highlight`).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('highlight')!,
  {
    highlight: false,
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Apples', 'Pears', 'Plums'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'y2025', name: '2025', data: [52, 31, 18] },
      { type: 'column', id: 'y2026', name: '2026', data: [47, 35, 22] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Interactions](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/interactions/): the tooltip and the highlight.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/legend/ -->

# legend

The list of series under the chart, each a button that hides or shows it.

Type: `LegendOptions | boolean`. Default: shown when there are two series or more.

## What it does

Each item is the series' sign (its colour and its marker, so it is not told by colour alone) and its name; a
series without a name is « Series 1 », « Series 2 »… Items are buttons: a click hides the series, which stays in the
legend, greyed, and a second click shows it again. Items wrap onto as many rows as needed.

`false` hides the legend; `true` shows it even for one series. An object places it: `position`, `'bottom'` (the
default), `'top'`, `'start'` or `'end'` (a column beside the plot, on the reading direction's start or end side); and
`align`, `'start'`, `'center'` (the default) or `'end'`.

A pie or a donut lists its slices instead, and shows its legend by default only when the labels beside the slices do
not fit.

Something else than a boolean or an object is `invalid-option` at `legend`; another key `unknown-option` at
`legend.<key>`; a wrong value `invalid-option` at `legend.position` or `legend.align`.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('legend')!,
  {
    legend: { position: 'end', align: 'start' },
    series: [
      { type: 'line', id: 'roses', name: 'Roses', data: [3, 4, 2, 5, 6] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'herbs', name: 'Herbs', data: [6, 5, 7, 6, 8] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`initiallyHidden`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/initially-hidden/): a series hidden when it first appears.
- [Interactions](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/interactions/): the legend with the tooltip and the keyboard.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/locale/ -->

# locale

The language numbers, dates and the chart's words are written in.

Type: `string`. Default: the page’s language (`lang`).

## What it does

A language tag (`'de-DE'`, `'fr'`, `'ar-EG'`), given to `Intl`: it writes the ticks, the tooltip, the data table
and the screen readers' labels — digits, separators, month names. It also chooses the chart's own words (« No data »,
the menu, the summary): English and French are built in, another language takes English unless `chart()` is given
[`messages`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/messages/).

Without it, the chart takes the `lang` of its element or of the closest parent that has one, else the browser's
language. A tag `Intl` does not accept is reported (`invalid-option` at `locale`) and the page's language is used.

The locale does not choose the time zone ([`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/)) nor the reading direction ([`dir`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/dir/)).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('locale')!,
  {
    locale: 'de-DE',
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['North', 'South', 'East'] },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'honey', name: 'Honey (kg)', data: [1234.5, 2875.25, 1980.75] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`dir`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/dir/): the reading direction.
- [Theming and right to left](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/theming-rtl/): the chart's words and right to left.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/ -->

# menu

A small menu for the reader: type, aggregation, scale, comparison, download, print.

Type: `boolean | { readonly items: readonly ('type' | 'aggregation' | 'scale' | 'compare' | 'export' | 'print')[] }`. Default: `false`. Needs the `menu` feature.

## What it does

A button at the end of the chart's top edge (« Chart options ») opens a menu. `true` offers every item; an object
lists those offered, in `items`: `'type'` (line, area or column for one series), `'aggregation'` (by period, on a time
axis), `'scale'` (linear or logarithmic, when every value is positive), `'compare'` (difference, percent, base 100),
`'export'` (a download as PNG, SVG or CSV) and `'print'`. An item shows only when it makes sense for the data; with
none left, the button is not shown. `'export'` and `'print'` need the [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/exporting/)
feature too.

The menu follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern: Enter, Space or ↓ open it, the arrows move, Escape closes it and
gives the focus back. A choice applies at once and is part of the [view](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): saved and given
back with it.

It needs the [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/menu/) feature (`missing-module` at `menu` without it). An `items` list that is
empty or names something else is `invalid-option` at `menu`.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, menu, exporting } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('menu')!,
  {
    menu: { items: ['type', 'scale', 'export'] },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'bees', name: 'Bees seen', data: [12, 30, 52, 61, 58, 44] }],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [menu, exporting] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/exporting/): what a download writes.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): comparison, aggregation and the menu.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/mirror/ -->

# mirror

In right to left, the x axis running right to left too.

Type: `boolean`. Default: `false`.

## What it does

Only right-to-left charts are concerned ([`dir`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/dir/) `'rtl'`, or the element's direction). By default
their x axis still runs left to right: time and categories flow as numbers do. `true` mirrors it: the first category,
the earliest time, is on the right. The value axis, the title and the legend follow the reading direction either way.

In left to right `mirror` changes nothing. A value other than a boolean is reported (`invalid-option` at `mirror`).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('mirror')!,
  {
    dir: 'rtl',
    mirror: true,
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Week 1', 'Week 2', 'Week 3', 'Week 4'] },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'jars', name: 'Jars', data: [18, 24, 21, 30] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`dir`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/dir/): the reading direction.
- [Theming and right to left](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/theming-rtl/): right to left.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/navigator/ -->

# navigator

A strip under the plot showing all the data and the visible window.

Type: `boolean`. Default: `false`. Needs the `navigatorStrip` feature.

## What it does

The strip (40 px, its own labels under it) draws the visible series over their whole x range, thin. A window marks
the range shown in the plot, the rest shaded. Drag the window to move the range, a handle to move one end; a click
outside the window moves it there. The two handles are sliders for the keyboard: the arrows move them by a hundredth of
the whole, Page Up and Page Down by a tenth, Shift moves the window. Zooming the plot moves the window, and the other
way round.

It needs the [`navigatorStrip`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/navigator-strip/) feature, which brings
[`zoom`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/zoom/). Without it the option is reported (`missing-module` at `navigator`) and no strip is
drawn. On a time axis the [range buttons](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/range-buttons/) come with it.

A value other than a boolean is reported (`invalid-option` at `navigator`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, timeAxis, navigatorStrip } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('navigator')!,
  {
    navigator: true,
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC' },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'level', name: 'Pond level (cm)', data: [['2026-01-01', 41], ['2026-02-01', 44], ['2026-03-01', 52], ['2026-04-01', 49]] }],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [timeAxis, navigatorStrip] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`rangeButtons`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/range-buttons/): spans of time with one click.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): zoom, the navigator and the view.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/range-buttons/ -->

# rangeButtons

Buttons for usual spans of time: a month, three months, the year so far, a year, all.

Type: `boolean`. Default: shown with the navigator, on a time axis. Needs the `navigatorStrip` feature.

## What it does

Above the plot, on the reading direction's start side: « 1m », « 3m », « YTD », « 1y », « All » (in the chart's
language). Each shows a span ending at the last point, counted on the axis's calendar and zone: one or three months
back, from 1 January of the last point's year, one year back; « All » goes back to the whole data. A button whose span
is longer than the data is disabled; the one matching the visible range is pressed.

They come by default with the [`navigator`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/navigator/) on a time axis; `false` leaves them out, `true` shows them
without the navigator. They need the [`navigatorStrip`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/navigator-strip/) feature (`missing-module` at
`rangeButtons` without it). They are spans of time: off a time axis they are reported (`not-available` at
`rangeButtons`, detail `not-time`) and left out. A value other than a boolean is `invalid-option`.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, timeAxis, navigatorStrip } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('range-buttons')!,
  {
    rangeButtons: true,
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC' },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'level', name: 'Pond level (cm)', data: [['2025-06-01', 38], ['2025-12-01', 47], ['2026-03-01', 52], ['2026-04-01', 49]] }],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [timeAxis, navigatorStrip] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`navigator`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/navigator/): the strip they come with.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): zoom, the navigator and the view.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/selection/ -->

# selection

Points the reader can select, with a rectangle, a range or a lasso.

Type: `boolean | { readonly shapes?: readonly ('rectangle' | 'range' | 'lasso')[] }`. Default: `false`. Needs the `selection` feature.

## What it does

`true` adds a « Select » mode to the chart's mode bar. In it, a drag selects with the current shape: a range of x
on charts of lines and areas, a rectangle on charts of marks (scatters, columns, bars). An object lists the shapes
offered, in `shapes`: `'rectangle'`, `'range'`, `'lasso'` (a free outline, exact even at a million points); with more
than one, the mode's button opens a choice.

A drag replaces the selection, Shift adds, Alt removes; a click selects one point, a click on empty plot or Escape
clears. With the keyboard, Space selects the focused point. Selected points keep their colour, the others fade; a
column or a slice gets a ring, so the selection is not told by colour alone. The selection is data, not pixels: it
survives zoom and resize, is part of the view, and the `selectionChange` event gives its count, indices and keys.

It needs the [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/selection/) feature (`missing-module` at `selection` without it). A `shapes`
list that is empty or names something else is `invalid-option` at `selection`.

## Example

```ts
import { scatter } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, selection } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('selection')!,
  {
    selection: { shapes: ['rectangle', 'lasso'] },
    series: [{ type: 'scatter', id: 'leaves', name: 'Leaves', data: [[2.1, 7.2], [2.8, 6.4], [3.5, 7.9], [5.9, 3.8], [6.4, 4.6], [7.1, 3.1]] }],
  },
  { types: [scatter], features: [selection] },
);

c.on('selectionChange', (e) => console.log(e.count));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`highlight`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/highlight/): the pointer's fading, which does not last.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): modes, selection and the view.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/series/ -->

# series

The series the chart draws: the only option it needs.

Type: `readonly SeriesOptions[]`. Required.

## What it does

A list of series, drawn in order. Each one has a `type`, which must be one of the `types` given to `chart()`,
and its `data`; the rest is optional. The keys every series has are under [Series](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/type/), and each
type's own under [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/line/).

Give each series an [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/id/) when series come and go: `update({ series })` matches the new list to
the old one by id, so a series that keeps its id keeps what the user did to it (hidden, selected) and moves from where
it was. `setData(id, data)` replaces one series' values without the rest.

A chart holds one kind of drawing. Lines, areas, columns, bars and scatters share axes and mix freely, except that
columns (upright) and bars (across) do not mix. A pie, a donut or a gauge is drawn alone.

What the chart reports, by series (`series[i]`):

- not a list: `invalid-option` at `series`, and nothing is drawn;
- a type the chart was not given: `unknown-series-type` at `series[i].type`, its name as the detail;
- a series of another kind than the first one: `invalid-option` at `series[i].type`; columns with bars:
  `mixed-orientation`;
- an id used twice, or starting with `#`: `duplicate-id` at `series[i].id`;
- a key it does not know: `unknown-option` at `series[i].<key>`.

A series reported this way is left out; the others are drawn.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('series')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'sold', name: 'Jars sold', data: [42, 38, 51, 47, 63] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'target', name: 'Target', data: [45, 45, 45, 50, 60] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column, line] },
);

c.setData('sold', [42, 38, 51, 47, 66]);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/id/): how series are matched.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/): each type and when to use it.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/title/ -->

# title

The chart's title, with a subtitle under it.

Type: `string | TitleOptions`.

## What it does

A string is the title. An object gives `text`, the title; `subtitle`, a smaller line under it; and `align`,
`'start'` (the default), `'center'` or `'end'`, along the reading direction: in right to left, `'start'` is on the
right.

The title is more than a heading. It names the chart for screen readers (the chart is a figure named by its title),
it heads an exported picture, and it names a downloaded file (letters, digits and hyphens kept), unless
[`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/exporting/) gives a `filename`.

A title that is neither a string nor an object with a `text` string is reported (`invalid-option` at `title`) and
left out. A key other than these three is reported (`unknown-option` at `title.<key>`), and so is a wrong `subtitle` or
`align` (`invalid-option` at `title.subtitle`, `title.align`).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('title')!,
  {
    title: { text: 'Jars of honey sold (made up)', subtitle: 'First half of the year', align: 'center' },
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'jars', name: 'Jars', data: [14, 22, 19, 27, 31, 26] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`description`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/description/): the sentence screen readers hear after the summary.
- [Export and print](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exporting/): the title in pictures and file names.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/x-axis/ -->

# xAxis

The axis along which the x values run.

Type: `AxisOptions | readonly AxisOptions[]`. Default: one axis, its scale guessed from the data.

## What it does

One axis, or a list of axes. Absent, the chart makes one, its scale guessed from the data: `'category'`
when the x values are strings, else `'linear'`. Each axis's keys have their page under [Axes](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/):
[`scale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/), [`min`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/min/) and [`max`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/max/),
[`ticks`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/ticks/), [`title`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/title/), [`opposite`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/),
[`reversed`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/reversed/), and the keys of one scale ([`categories`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/categories/),
[`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/)).

With several axes, the first is `x`, the next `x2`, `x3`… unless an axis has an [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/id/); a series
names the one it is drawn against ([`xAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/x-axis/)). An id is shared by x and y axes: two axes may not have
the same one (`duplicate-id`).

An x axis may group its points by period or step ([`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/)); a value axis's keys
(`stacking`, `compare`) are refused on it (`invalid-option`). A `'time'` scale needs the
[`timeAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/time-axis/) feature.

Problems name the axis by its place, even when one axis is given alone: `xAxis[0]`. An axis that is not an object is
`invalid-option` at `xAxis[i]`; a key the axis's scale does not have is `unknown-option` at `xAxis[i].<key>`.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('x-axis')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', title: 'Month', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'visits', name: 'Visits', data: [310, 340, 420, 510, 580, 640] }],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`yAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/y-axis/): the value axes.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): scales, bounds, ticks and time.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/y-axis/ -->

# yAxis

The value axis, or several of them.

Type: `AxisOptions | readonly AxisOptions[]`. Default: one axis, its scale guessed from the data.

## What it does

One axis, or a list of axes. Absent, the chart makes one, its scale guessed from the data: `'category'`
when the y values are strings, else `'linear'`. Each axis's keys have their page under [Axes](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/):
[`scale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/), [`min`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/min/) and [`max`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/max/),
[`ticks`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/ticks/), [`title`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/title/), [`opposite`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/),
[`reversed`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/reversed/), and the keys of one scale ([`categories`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/categories/),
[`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/)).

With several axes, the first is `y`, the next `y2`, `y3`… unless an axis has an [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/id/); a series
names the one it is drawn against ([`yAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/y-axis/)). An id is shared by x and y axes: two axes may not have
the same one (`duplicate-id`).

A value axis may show its piles as shares ([`stacking`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/stacking/)) and compare each series to a
baseline ([`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/)). Two value axes: give the second `opposite: true` to put it on the far
side; its ticks fall on the first one's gridlines, and each axis shows the signs of its series before its title.

Problems name the axis by its place, even when one axis is given alone: `yAxis[0]`. An axis that is not an object is
`invalid-option` at `yAxis[i]`; a key the axis's scale does not have is `unknown-option` at `yAxis[i].<key>`.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('y-axis')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
    yAxis: [{ title: 'Rain (mm)' }, { title: 'Temperature (°C)', opposite: true }],
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain', data: [62, 48, 51, 44, 57, 39] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'warmth', name: 'Temperature', yAxis: 'y2', data: [4, 6, 9, 12, 16, 19] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column, line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`xAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/x-axis/): the axis of the x values.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): two value axes, log scale, bounds.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/aggregate/ -->

# aggregate

How the series sums up its points, when the x axis groups them by period or by bucket.

Type: `'sum' | 'mean' | 'min' | 'max' | 'count'`. Default: `'sum'` for columns and bars, `'mean'` otherwise.

## What it does

Used only when the x axis aggregates: by its [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/) option, or by the user's choice in
the [menu](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/). Each period, or bucket, becomes one point: `'sum'` of its values, their `'mean'`,
their `'min'`, their `'max'`, or the `'count'` of its points. Gaps count for nothing, and a period without points is a
gap, not a zero. The tooltip names the period and says how many points it holds. Another value is reported as
`invalid-option` (`series[i].aggregate`) and the default is used.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { aggregation, chart, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('sensor')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC', aggregate: 'day' },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'sensor', name: 'Highest reading', aggregate: 'max', data: [['2026-01-01T09:00Z', 4], ['2026-01-01T15:00Z', 7], ['2026-01-02T11:00Z', 5]] }],
  },
  { types: [column], features: [aggregation, timeAxis] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/) on the axis: the periods or buckets.
- [`aggregation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/), the feature.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): aggregation.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/color/ -->

# color

The series' colour: a place in the theme's palette, or a colour of your own, defined in CSS.

Type: `SeriesColor`. Default: the palette’s next colour, by position.

## What it does

A number is a place in the theme's palette, counting from 1 (`--dzgraph-series-1`); past the eighth it starts again
from the first. `{ token: 'brand' }` is a colour you define in CSS as `--dzgraph-color-brand` (the name a CSS
identifier), so light and dark mode and your contrast checks hold:

```css
.sales-chart {
  --dzgraph-color-brand: var(--my-brand-color);
}
```

Colours are never written in the options. Anything else (`0`, `2.5`, a name that is not a CSS identifier) is
reported as `invalid-option` (`series[i].color`), and the series keeps its place's colour. Colour is never the only
way to tell series apart: each also has its marker symbol and its sign in the legend.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('jam')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'plum', name: 'Plum', color: 3, data: [14, 22, 19] },
      { type: 'column', id: 'quince', name: 'Quince', color: { token: 'brand' }, data: [9, 12, 17] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Theming and right to left](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/theming-rtl/): the palette and its variables.
- [Accessibility](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/accessibility/): never colour alone.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/data/ -->

# data

The series' values, in one of four shapes.

Type: `D`. Required.

## What it does

- **Values alone**, `[3, 5, null, 4]`: x is each value's place, or the axis's categories in order.
- **Pairs**, `[[x, y], …]`: x a number, a string (a category, or a date-time on a time axis), y a number.
- **Points**, `[{ x, y, key, name }, …]`: `key` is the point's identity (for a drilldown, a DzGrid row, a linked
  chart); `name` replaces x in the tooltip and the data table.
- **Columns**, `{ x, y, key }`: one array per field, the same length; the fastest shape for a big series. A typed `y`
  (`Float64Array`) is read without a copy, and `NaN` in it is a gap.

`null` is a gap: a line breaks there, a column is missing. A pie takes slices (`[['Apples', 120], …]`) and a gauge
one value (`72`): see [`pie`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/pie/) and [`gauge`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/gauge/).

Bad values never throw: each kind of fault becomes a gap, reported once for the series with its first place and its
count, never the value. A value that is not a number is `invalid-data` (`series[i].data[3]`, `count=2`); `Infinity`
is `non-finite-value`; a repeated key is `duplicate-key`; columns of different lengths are `invalid-data` with
`length`. On a line or an area, x going backwards is drawn as given and reported (`unsorted-x`). `setData()` replaces
the values alone, the cheapest update.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('shapes')!,
  {
    series: [
      { type: 'line', id: 'values', name: 'Values', data: [3, 5, null, 4, 6] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'pairs', name: 'Pairs', data: [[0, 2], [1, 3], [3, 2.5], [4, 4]] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'points', name: 'Points', data: [{ x: 0, y: 1, key: 'start' }, { x: 2, y: 1.5, name: 'Middle' }, { x: 4, y: 2 }] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'columns', name: 'Columns', data: { x: new Float64Array([0, 1, 2, 3, 4]), y: new Float64Array([6, 6.5, 7, 6, 7.5]) } },
    ],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Data](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/data/): every shape, gaps and keys, in detail.
- [Big data](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/big-data/): typed columns at a million points.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/drilldown/ -->

# drilldown

Each point's detail: a click on the point shows it in its place.

Type: `{ readonly details: Readonly<Record<string, readonly SeriesOptions[]>> } | { readonly load: (point: PointRef) => Promise<readonly SeriesOptions[]> }`. Needs the `drilldown` feature.

## What it does

`{ details: { [key]: series[] } }` gives the detail of each point by its [key](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/data/); `{ load: (point) =>
Promise<series[]> }` loads it when asked. A point with a detail shows a hand under the pointer, and screen readers
hear « detail available ». A click, or Enter, replaces the chart's series by the detail's; a breadcrumb above the plot
goes back, as do Backspace and Alt + ←, and the level comes back as it was. The event `drill` gives the path of keys,
and the view keeps it. A load that fails, or takes more than 10 s, says so and offers to retry.

Anything but exactly one of `details` (each a list of series) or `load` (a function) is reported as `invalid-option`
(`series[i].drilldown`). Without the `drilldown` feature the option is reported (`missing-module`) and no point has a
detail.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, drilldown } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('orchard')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Apples', 'Pears'] },
    series: [
      {
        type: 'column',
        id: 'fruit',
        name: 'Crates',
        data: { y: [52, 31], key: ['apples', 'pears'] },
        drilldown: {
          details: {
            apples: [{ type: 'column', id: 'apples', name: 'Apples', data: [['Gala', 22], ['Russet', 17], ['Bramley', 13]] }],
            pears: [{ type: 'column', id: 'pears', name: 'Pears', data: [['Comice', 19], ['Conference', 12]] }],
          },
        },
      },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column], features: [drilldown] },
);
c.on('drill', (e) => console.log(e.path));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/drilldown/) on the chart: years, months, days on a time axis.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): drilldown with the other ways to explore.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/id/ -->

# id

The series' identity: how updates, the view, links and events recognise it.

Type: `string`. Default: `#1`, `#2`… by position.

## What it does

`update()` matches series by `id`: a series that keeps its id keeps what the user did to it (hidden, selected
points) and moves from where it was. `setData()` and `setSeriesVisible()` name it; events give it as `seriesId`; the
view saves hidden series and selections under it; linked charts and DzGrid find points through it.

Absent, a series is `#1`, `#2`… by its position, so a series that moves changes identity: give ids when series come
and go. `#` is reserved for these. An id that starts with `#`, or one already used, is reported as `duplicate-id`
(`series[i].id`), and the series takes its position's id; an id that is not a string is `invalid-option`. Every other
problem of the series carries its id (`seriesId`).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('jars')!,
  {
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'jars', name: 'Jars sold', data: [14, 22, 19] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
c.setData('jars', [14, 22, 19, 27]);
c.setSeriesVisible('jars', false);
```

## See also

- [`name`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/name/): what the reader sees.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the view, saved by series id.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/initially-hidden/ -->

# initiallyHidden

The series starts hidden; the reader shows it from the legend.

Type: `boolean`. Default: `false`.

## What it does

Read once per series id, when a series of that id first appears. Afterwards hiding is the user's: the legend, the
view and `setSeriesVisible()` decide, and options given again (a signal rebuilding them, `update()`) never undo what
the user did. A hidden series keeps its item in the legend, greyed, and its colour for when it comes back; it
leaves the tooltip, the data table and the axes' ranges. A value that is not a boolean is reported as
`invalid-option` (`series[i].initiallyHidden`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('beds')!,
  {
    series: [
      { type: 'line', id: 'roses', name: 'Roses', data: [3, 4, 2, 5] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'herbs', name: 'Herbs', data: [6, 5, 7, 6] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'beans', name: 'Beans', initiallyHidden: true, data: [2, 3, 3, 4] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/id/): what « first appears » is counted by.
- [Interactions](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/interactions/): the legend.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/name/ -->

# name

The series' name, shown in the legend, the tooltip and the data table, and read by screen readers.

Type: `string`. Default: « Series 1 », « Series 2 »… in the chart’s language.

## What it does

Text, written as given. A name in another script keeps its own direction (« مبيعات » reads right to left in a left
to right chart). Absent, the chart names the series by its place, in its own language: « Series 2 » here, « Série 2 »
on a French page; the `seriesName` words of `messages` change that. A name that is not a string is reported as
`invalid-option` (`series[i].name`).

The name is what a reader sees, not an identity: [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/id/) is what updates and the view use.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('bees')!,
  {
    series: [
      { type: 'line', id: 'hiveA', name: 'Hive A', data: [12, 18, 26, 31] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'hiveB', data: [8, 11, 19, 24] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/id/): the series' identity.
- [`messages`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/messages/): the chart's own words.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/type/ -->

# type

The series' type: how it is drawn, and which options of its own it takes.

Type: `T`. Required.

## What it does

`'line'`, `'area'`, `'column'`, `'bar'`, `'scatter'`, `'pie'`, `'donut'` or `'gauge'`: the name of a type given to the
chart in `types` (`allTypes` gives them all). Each type has its page, with its own options:
[`line`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/line/), [`column`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/column/), [`pie`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/pie/)…

A name the chart was not given leaves the series out, reported as `unknown-series-type` with the name as detail. A
chart has one coordinate system, its first series': lines, areas, columns, bars and scatters mix on axes, while a
pie, a donut or a gauge stands alone. A series that does not fit is left out and reported (`invalid-option` on
`series[i].type`). Columns and bars set the chart's orientation: one of each is `mixed-orientation`.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('rain')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain (mm)', data: [62, 48, 51, 44] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'trend', name: 'Trend (mm)', data: [58, 54, 50, 47] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column, line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`types`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/types/): the types a chart may draw.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/): every type, with live charts.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/x-axis/ -->

# xAxis

The x axis the series is drawn against, named by the axis's id.

Type: `string`. Default: the first axis.

## What it does

Axis ids are given by [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/id/) on the axis, or are `x`, then `x2`, `x3`… by position; x and y axes share
one set of ids. An id no x axis has is reported as `unknown-axis`, with the id as detail, and the series goes on the
first x axis. On a bar chart the x axis runs upright, but it is still the series' `xAxis`.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('honey')!,
  {
    xAxis: { id: 'months', scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar'] },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'honey', name: 'Honey (kg)', xAxis: 'months', data: [14, 22, 19] }],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## See also

- [`yAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/y-axis/): the value axis.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/y-axis/ -->

# yAxis

The value axis the series is drawn against, named by the axis's id.

Type: `string`. Default: the first axis.

## What it does

Two measures of different units go on two value axes: give the y axes ids and name one from each series. With two
value axes in use, each axis shows the signs of its series, so the reader knows which axis a line is read on. Ids are
`y`, `y2`… by position when the axes have none. An id no y axis has is reported as `unknown-axis`, with the id as
detail, and the series goes on the first y axis.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('weather')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr'] },
    yAxis: [{ id: 'rain', title: 'Rain (mm)' }, { id: 'warmth', title: 'Temperature (°C)', opposite: true }],
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain', yAxis: 'rain', data: [62, 48, 51, 44] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'warmth', name: 'Temperature', yAxis: 'warmth', data: [4, 6, 9, 12] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column, line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`xAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/x-axis/): the x axis.
- [`opposite`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/): an axis on the far side.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): two value axes.
