<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/area/ -->

# area

A line with its surface filled down to zero.

Import: `area` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `AreaSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

An area is a [line](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/line/) whose surface is filled down to zero, translucent, with the line on top; below zero it
fills up to zero. Its axis always holds zero. `marker` works as on a line.

`stack` piles the area on the other areas of the same stack: `true` is the stack named `default`, a string names
another. Areas pile by equal x values, a missing point counting as zero there; the value axis takes the piles in.
`stacking: 'percent'` on the y axis turns each pile into shares of its total. Stacked areas are not decimated. A
`stack` that is not a boolean or a non-empty string is `invalid-option` (`series[i].stack`), and so is a stack on a
log axis.

## Example

```ts
import { area } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('visits')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'area', id: 'greenhouse', name: 'Greenhouse', stack: true, data: [42, 46, 61, 58, 70] },
      { type: 'area', id: 'orchard', name: 'Orchard', stack: true, data: [12, 15, 30, 26, 41] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [area] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`line`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/line/): the same without the fill.
- [`stacking`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/stacking/): piles as shares.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/): stacks.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/bar/ -->

# bar

Columns turned across: the chart becomes horizontal.

Import: `bar` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `BarSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

Bars are [columns](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/column/) turned across. The categories run down from the top; the values grow along the reading
direction, from the left in left to right, from the right in right to left. The x axis is upright and the value axis
across, but they keep their names: categories are still `xAxis`, values `yAxis`. Lines, areas and scatters in the
same chart follow the bars' orientation; columns in it are reported (`mixed-orientation`).

`stack` works as on columns.

## Example

```ts
import { bar } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('jars')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Plum', 'Quince', 'Cherry'] },
    series: [{ type: 'bar', id: 'jars', name: 'Jars sold', data: [1250, 860, 2240] }],
  },
  { types: [bar] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`column`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/column/): the same, upright.
- [Theming and right to left](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/theming-rtl/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/column/ -->

# column

Upright rectangles from zero, side by side in each category's band.

Import: `column` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `ColumnSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

Each category has a band along the axis; the series' columns stand side by side in it, in series order. Columns start
at zero, from a stronger zero line: positive ones rise, negative ones go down. A value that is not zero is at least
1 px high, and zero draws no column. The free end is rounded, the base straight. Hidden series give their room back.
A chart with columns is upright: bars in the same chart are reported (`mixed-orientation`).

`stack` piles the column on the others of the same stack (`true`: the stack `default`); several stacks stand side
by side in each band. Positive values pile upwards, negative ones downwards. With `aggregate` on the x axis, columns
sum their points by default.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('harvest')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'apples', name: 'Apples', data: [5, 8, 6, -2] },
      { type: 'column', id: 'pears', name: 'Pears', data: [1, 2, 3, 4] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`bar`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/bar/): the same, across.
- [`stacking`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/stacking/): piles as shares.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/donut/ -->

# donut

A pie with a hole, which holds the total.

Import: `donut` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `DonutSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

Everything a [pie](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/pie/) does, `others` included, with a hole in the middle. `hole` is its size as a share of the
radius, from 0 to 0.9; anything else is reported (`invalid-option`, `series[i].hole`). The hole shows the total and
the word « Total »; `center: { label, value }` writes your own words (both strings), and `center: false` leaves it
empty. A `center` of another shape is `invalid-option` (`series[i].center`).

## Example

```ts
import { donut } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('seeds')!,
  {
    series: [
      {
        type: 'donut',
        id: 'seeds',
        name: 'Seeds',
        hole: 0.5,
        center: { label: 'Packets', value: '1 400' },
        data: [['Carrots', 420], ['Beetroot', 260], ['Lettuce', 380], ['Radishes', 190], ['Spinach', 150]],
      },
    ],
  },
  { types: [donut] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`pie`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/pie/): the slices, their labels and « Others ».
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/gauge/ -->

# gauge

One value on a half ring, or on a bar, from `min` to `max`.

Import: `gauge` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `GaugeSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

`data` is one value (`640`, or `[640]`); anything else is reported as `invalid-data` (`series[i].data`), and `null`
shows an empty track and « — ». The half ring fills from `min` to the value along the reading direction; the value is
written large under it, `min` and `max` at its ends. A value past the scale fills the arc, and the text shows the real
value. `min` not below `max` is reported (`invalid-option`, `series[i].min`) and the scale goes back to 0–100.

`thresholds` draw a thin ring of ranges just outside the arc: each `{ from, to, label, color }`, `from` below `to`.
The `label` of the range the value falls in is written under the value, so it is not told by colour alone. `color`
names a colour you define in CSS as `--dzgraph-color-<name>` (here `--dzgraph-color-low`); without it the range is
neutral. A threshold of another shape is `invalid-option` (`series[i].thresholds[0]`). A gauge stands alone and has no
legend by default: its title names it.

## A scale either side of zero

Three options make a richer gauge; a gauge without them is drawn as above.

- `origin` is where the fill starts (by default `min`). With `origin: 0` on a scale from −2000 to 2000, a value below
  zero fills towards the left end, one above towards the right end (in right to left, the other way round). An origin
  off the scale is `invalid-option` (`series[i].origin`) and `min` is used.
- `ticks: { step, labels }` draws a short tick inside the arc at every multiple of `step`, and a longer one with its
  number at every multiple of `labels`. The numbers then write the scale's ends, so they are not written twice. A
  number that would cover the value is left out. A `step` that is not a positive number, or that would draw more than
  200 ticks, is `invalid-option` (`series[i].ticks.step`) and no tick is drawn; a `labels` that is not a multiple of
  `step` (`series[i].ticks.labels`) gives no numbers.
- `thresholdsOn: 'track'` paints the thresholds on the arc itself, the whole thickness, and writes each one's label
  around the arc at its middle. The value becomes a narrower arc, edged with the background, so the zones show on both
  its sides. The value's own zone is still named under the value. Labels that would overlap: the later one is left out.

Ticks and zone labels are pictures of the scale and the thresholds: screen readers, the tooltip and the data table say
the value, the scale and the threshold, as before.

```ts
import { gauge } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('balance')!,
  {
    series: [
      {
        type: 'gauge',
        id: 'balance',
        name: 'Tank balance',
        data: -1700,
        min: -2000,
        max: 2000,
        origin: 0,
        ticks: { step: 100, labels: 500 },
        thresholdsOn: 'track',
        thresholds: [
          { from: -2000, to: -1500, label: 'Cold', color: 'cold' },
          { from: -500, to: 500, label: 'Normal', color: 'calm' },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  { types: [gauge] },
);
```

The colour names are yours to define. Set them on the chart's root, `.dzgraph`, when they take a colour of the chart's
own palette (its variables live there):

```css
#balance .dzgraph {
  --dzgraph-color-cold: var(--dzgraph-series-3);
  --dzgraph-color-calm: var(--dzgraph-series-4);
}
```

## As a bar

`shape: 'bar'` draws the same gauge as a straight bar; every option above holds for it. `orientation: 'vertical'`
stands it upright, as a thermometer (by default it lies across). Across, `min` is at the reading direction's start
(on the right in right to left); upright, `min` is at the bottom. Another word for either is `invalid-option`
(`series[i].shape`, `series[i].orientation`): the arc is drawn, or the bar lies across.

Across, the value is written on top with its zone's label, then the zones' labels, the bar, and the ticks and their
numbers under it. Upright, the ticks and numbers are on the inline-end side, the zones' labels on the other. Numbers
that would overlap are left out (the later one). The bar is 24 px thick at most.

```ts
import type { GaugeSeriesOptions } from '@dzgraph/core';

const balance: GaugeSeriesOptions = {
  type: 'gauge',
  shape: 'bar', // orientation: 'vertical' to stand it upright
  min: -2000,
  max: 2000,
  origin: 0,
  data: -1700,
  ticks: { step: 100, labels: 500 },
  thresholdsOn: 'track',
  thresholds: [], // as above
};
```

## Try it

Set each part with its buttons, or type a number or a name: the gauge follows, and its options are written under
it, ready to copy. `thickness` sets the arc's or the bar's thickness in pixels (by default a quarter of the radius for
the arc, 24 px for the bar); a box too small for it gives what room it has, and a value that is not a positive
number is `invalid-option` (`series[i].thickness`).

## Example

```ts
import { gauge } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('tank')!,
  {
    series: [
      {
        type: 'gauge',
        id: 'tank',
        name: 'Water tank (litres)',
        data: 640,
        min: 0,
        max: 1000,
        thresholds: [
          { from: 0, to: 200, label: 'Low', color: 'low' },
          { from: 200, to: 800, label: 'Fine' },
          { from: 800, to: 1000, label: 'Full' },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  { types: [gauge] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`color`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/color/): colours you define in CSS.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/line/ -->

# line

Points joined in x order by straight segments.

Import: `line` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `LineSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

The points are joined in x order; a gap (`null`) breaks the line, and a point alone between two gaps shows as a
marker. Markers show on every point when the points are far enough apart to read them; a denser line keeps one about
every 80 px, each series at its own offset. `marker: true` puts one on every point, `false` none. Each series has its
own marker symbol (circle, square, diamond, triangle…), so lines are told apart without colour.

A line with more points than the plot has pixel columns is drawn from far fewer points that look the same (every
column's highest and lowest point kept); the tooltip and the data table show the real points. x going backwards is
drawn in the order given and reported once (`unsorted-x`). Lines do not stack: `stack` on a line is
`unknown-option`. A `marker` that is not a boolean is `invalid-option` (`series[i].marker`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('bees')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['08:00', '10:00', '12:00', '14:00', '16:00', '18:00'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'line', id: 'hiveA', name: 'Hive A', data: [12, 30, null, 61, 44, 23] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'hiveB', name: 'Hive B', marker: false, data: [8, 21, 39, 47, 35, 15] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [line] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`area`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/area/): a line filled down to zero.
- [`data`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/data/): the shapes of the values.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/pie/ -->

# pie

The parts of one whole, as slices.

Import: `pie` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `PieSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

Slices are pairs (`['Carrots', 420]`), points (`{ name, y, key }`) or values alone, named by their place (« Slice
3 »), one shape per series. Each slice's angle is its share of the total; the first starts at the top and the others follow clockwise, in
data order. Zero gives no slice and `null` is a gap; a negative value cannot be a part of a whole and is reported
(`invalid-data`). Each slice is labelled outside with its name and its share, joined by a leader line; when the labels
do not fit, the legend shows instead.

`others`: past seven slices, the six largest stay and the rest join one slice « Others », drawn last in a neutral
colour, with any slice under 2 % of the total; its tooltip lists its slices. `others: false` keeps every slice. A pie
stands alone: one pie, donut or gauge per chart, without axes.

## Example

```ts
import { pie } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('seeds')!,
  {
    series: [
      {
        type: 'pie',
        id: 'seeds',
        name: 'Seeds',
        data: [['Carrots', 420], ['Beetroot', 260], ['Lettuce', 380], ['Radishes', 190], ['Spinach', 150]],
      },
    ],
  },
  { types: [pie] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`donut`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/donut/): a pie with a hole.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/scatter/ -->

# scatter

One marker per point, placed by its x and its y.

Import: `scatter` from `@dzgraph/core`. Options: `ScatterSeriesOptions`.

## What it draws

Both axes are value axes fitted to the data, rounded to ticks; zero is not forced in. Each point is an 8 px marker
of the series' symbol, slightly translucent so that piles of points read darker. A point with a gap in either value is
left out. x need not be sorted. Each marker has its own tooltip. Past 2 000 markers the series is painted on a Canvas
(the `canvas` feature), past 100 000 with WebGL2 (`webgl`), with the same look.

## Example

```ts
import { scatter } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { canvas, chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('leaves')!,
  {
    xAxis: { title: 'Length (cm)' },
    yAxis: { title: 'Width (cm)' },
    series: [{ type: 'scatter', id: 'leaves', name: 'Leaves', data: [[4.2, 2.1], [5.0, 2.6], [6.3, 3.0], [3.8, 1.7]] }],
  },
  { types: [scatter], features: [canvas] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`canvas`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/canvas/) and [`webgl`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/webgl/): the painters for many points.
- [Big data](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/big-data/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/ -->

# aggregate

One point per period, or per bucket of values, on an x axis.

Type: `undefined`. Needs the `aggregation` feature.

## What it does

On an x axis, with the [`aggregation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/) feature:

- on a time axis, a period of the zone's calendar: `'hour'`, `'day'`, `'week'` (from Monday), `'month'`,
  `'quarter'` or `'year'`;
- on a numeric axis, `{ step }`: buckets of that width (`{ step: 10 }`: 0–10, 10–20…).

Each series becomes one point per group, at the group's start, its value the series'
[`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/aggregate/) function of the points in it (sum for columns and bars, mean otherwise). A
period without points is a gap. The axis keeps its own ticks. The tooltip names the period and how many points it
holds; the data table lists the groups; selecting a group selects every point in it.

Reported (`invalid-option` at `xAxis[0].aggregate`) and left out: on a y axis, on a category axis, a period on a
numeric axis, a step on a time axis. The chart's [menu](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/) can offer the periods to the user; the view
keeps the choice, which wins over the option. [`drilldown: 'time'`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/drilldown/) starts from years
whatever this option says.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, aggregation, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('rain')!, {
  xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'Europe/Paris', aggregate: 'week' },
  series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain (mm)', aggregate: 'sum', data: [['2026-03-02', 4], ['2026-03-04', 11], ['2026-03-10', 7], ['2026-03-18', 2]] }],
}, { types: [column], features: [timeAxis, aggregation] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/aggregate/), the series' function.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): aggregation and drilldown.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/categories/ -->

# categories

A category axis's categories, in order.

Type: `undefined`. Default: the data’s, in order of appearance.

## What it does

One band per category, its label centred under it. A series of plain values puts its first value in the first
category, and so on; a series of `[name, value]` pairs or points with a string `x` finds its category by name. A
category given twice is kept once.

Without the list, the categories are collected from the data, in order of appearance. With it, a name the list does
not hold gets a band of its own after the others, and a value past the last category a band named by its position;
both are reported once per series (`invalid-data`). Labels that do not fit turn by 45°, then every second (third…)
one shows, then a long one ends with « … » and shows whole in the tooltip.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('crates')!, {
  title: { text: 'Crates picked (made up)' },
  xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Apples', 'Pears', 'Plums', 'Cherries'] },
  series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'crates', name: 'Crates', data: [52, 31, 18, 44] }],
}, { types: [column] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`scale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/): the category scale and the others.
- [Data](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/data/): the shapes a series takes.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare-to/ -->

# compareTo

A fixed baseline for the comparison, at an x value.

Type: `undefined`. Default: the first point in view.

## What it does

With [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/) on the same y axis: each series is compared to its point at that x, or the last
one before it. A fixed baseline does not move when the user zooms or pans. The x is a number, or on a time x axis an
ISO date-time with an offset, read in the axis's [zone](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/).

A value of another kind is reported (`invalid-option` at `yAxis[0].compareTo`). Without `compare`, the comparison has
no mode: reported at `yAxis[0].compare`.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, compare, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('jars')!, {
  title: { text: 'Jars sold, compared with 4 March (made up)' },
  xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC' },
  yAxis: { compare: 'percent', compareTo: '2026-03-04T00:00:00Z' },
  series: [
    { type: 'line', id: 'plum', name: 'Plum', data: [['2026-03-02', 40], ['2026-03-03', 44], ['2026-03-04', 50], ['2026-03-05', 47], ['2026-03-06', 58], ['2026-03-07', 61]] },
    { type: 'line', id: 'quince', name: 'Quince', data: [['2026-03-02', 22], ['2026-03-03', 21], ['2026-03-04', 20], ['2026-03-05', 26], ['2026-03-06', 25], ['2026-03-07', 29]] },
  ],
}, { types: [line], features: [timeAxis, compare] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/): the modes.
- [`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/): how a date-time is read.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/ -->

# compare

Each series on this y axis shown against its baseline.

Type: `undefined`. Needs the `compare` feature.

## What it does

On a y axis, with the [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/compare/) feature:

- `'value'`: the difference, y − base; the axis is signed (+10, −5).
- `'percent'`: the change in percent, (y / base − 1) × 100; the axis is signed (+12 %).
- `'index'`: base 100, y / base × 100.

The baseline is each series' first point with a value in the visible range: zooming or panning moves it.
[`compareTo`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare-to/) fixes it. A line marks the reference (0, 0 % or 100). The tooltip and the data table
give the compared value, then the raw one.

A series that cannot be compared (no point at or before the baseline, or a base of 0 for a percent or an index) is not
drawn and is reported `no-baseline` until the range gives it one. Reported (`invalid-option` at `yAxis[0].compare`)
and left out: on an x axis, a log axis, or an axis with stacked series. The chart's [menu](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/) can offer
the comparison to the user; the view keeps the choice, which wins over the option.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, compare } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('shops')!, {
  title: { text: 'Two made-up shops, compared with January' },
  xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
  yAxis: { compare: 'percent' },
  series: [
    { type: 'line', id: 'north', name: 'North shop', data: [210, 231, 224, 262, 282, 277] },
    { type: 'line', id: 'south', name: 'South shop', data: [90, 88, 101, 111, 109, 126] },
  ],
}, { types: [line], features: [compare] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`compareTo`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare-to/): a fixed baseline.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): comparing, with the other ways to explore.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/id/ -->

# id

The name series use to sit on this axis.

Type: `undefined`. Default: `x` and `y`, then `x2`, `y2`….

## What it does

A series picks its axes by id: its [`xAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/x-axis/) and [`yAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/y-axis/). A
series that names none sits on the first x axis and the first y axis. Give ids as soon as there are two axes of a
kind: the ids say which series goes where, whatever the order of the list.

Two axes of one kind with the same id: the second keeps its default id, reported `duplicate-id` (`yAxis[1].id`). A
series naming an axis that does not exist is drawn on the first one, reported `unknown-axis` with the id it asked for.
The x axis's id also names it in the view: the visible range is kept by axis id.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('rain')!, {
  xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
  yAxis: [{ id: 'rain', title: 'Rain (mm)' }, { id: 'heat', title: 'Warmth (°C)', opposite: true }],
  series: [
    { type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain', yAxis: 'rain', data: [62, 48, 51, 44, 57, 39] },
    { type: 'line', id: 'heat', name: 'Warmth', yAxis: 'heat', data: [4, 6, 9, 13, 17, 21] },
  ],
}, { types: [column, line] });
```

## See also

- [`opposite`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/): the second value axis on the far side.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): two value axes.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/max/ -->

# max

The axis's upper bound, fixed.

Type: `undefined`. Default: from the data, rounded to ticks.

## What it does

Kept exactly, not rounded: a share drawn up to `100` shows how far it is from full. The other end is still
fitted to the data and rounded to a tick. A `max` below every value of the data is reported (`invalid-option`) and
left out. A zoom stays within the bounds.

On a time axis a bound is milliseconds, an ISO date-time with an offset, or a day (`'2026-03-01'`, its
midnight in the axis's [zone](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/)); a date-time without an offset is reported `ambiguous-instant` and left out.
On a log axis a bound of zero or below is reported (`invalid-option`) and left out. A `min` at or above `max` is
reported at `min`, and both are left out. A category axis has no bounds: they are reported (`unknown-option`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('charge')!, {
  title: { text: 'A made-up battery' },
  yAxis: { max: 100, title: 'Charge (%)' },
  series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'charge', name: 'Charge', data: [48, 41, 33, 27, 19, 12] }],
}, { types: [line] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`min`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/min/): the lower bound.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/min/ -->

# min

The axis's lower bound, fixed.

Type: `undefined`. Default: from the data, rounded to ticks.

## What it does

Without it, a value axis fits the data and rounds its ends outwards to ticks; columns, bars and areas always keep
zero in. A `min` is kept exactly, not rounded; the other end is still rounded to a tick, and the ticks fall inside.
A `min` above every value of the data is reported (`invalid-option`) and left out. A zoom stays within the bounds.

On a time axis a bound is milliseconds, an ISO date-time with an offset, or a day (`'2026-03-01'`, its
midnight in the axis's [zone](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/)); a date-time without an offset is reported `ambiguous-instant` and left out.
On a log axis a bound of zero or below is reported (`invalid-option`) and left out. A `min` at or above `max` is
reported at `min`, and both are left out. A category axis has no bounds: they are reported (`unknown-option`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('visits')!, {
  title: { text: 'Visitors a day (made up)' },
  yAxis: { min: 0 },
  series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'visits', name: 'Visitors', data: [64, 71, 69, 78, 87, 82, 75] }],
}, { types: [line] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`max`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/max/): the upper bound.
- [`ticks`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/ticks/): how many, and their labels.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/ -->

# opposite

The axis on the far side of the plot.

Type: `undefined`. Default: `false`.

## What it does

An x axis goes to the top instead of the bottom; a y axis to the end of the reading direction instead of its
start: the right in a left-to-right page, the left in a right-to-left one. It holds whatever the orientation: with
bars, the x axis runs upright and `opposite` moves it to the end side.

Its usual use is a second value axis. The second axis's ticks then fall on the first one's gridlines (same count, its
own round step), so one set of gridlines serves both; only the first draws them.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('rain')!, {
  xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
  yAxis: [{ id: 'rain', title: 'Rain (mm)' }, { id: 'heat', title: 'Warmth (°C)', opposite: true }],
  series: [
    { type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain', yAxis: 'rain', data: [62, 48, 51, 44, 57, 39] },
    { type: 'line', id: 'heat', name: 'Warmth', yAxis: 'heat', data: [4, 6, 9, 13, 17, 21] },
  ],
}, { types: [column, line] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`id`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/id/): which series sits on which axis.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): two value axes.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/reversed/ -->

# reversed

The axis drawn from its end to its start.

Type: `undefined`. Default: `false`.

## What it does

Values grow towards the origin: on a y axis, downwards (a depth, a rank where 1 is best); on an x axis, from the
end of the reading direction to its start. Every other rule stays: rounded ends, ticks, zero kept for columns and
areas, which now grow from the top. On a log axis it works the same.

## Example

```ts
import { area } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('lake')!, {
  title: { text: 'A made-up lake, crossed' },
  xAxis: { title: 'Distance from the shore (m)' },
  yAxis: { title: 'Depth (m)', reversed: true },
  series: [{ type: 'area', id: 'depth', name: 'Depth', data: [[0, 0], [20, 3.5], [40, 8.2], [60, 12.4], [80, 9.1], [100, 2.6], [120, 0]] }],
}, { types: [area] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`opposite`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/): the axis on the far side.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/).

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/ -->

# scale

How the axis turns values into positions.

Type: `undefined`. Default: `'linear'`, or `'category'` when the x values are strings.

## What it does

- `'linear'`: numbers, equal steps for equal differences.
- `'log'`: base ten, each power of ten the same length; for values spread over several orders of magnitude. On a value
  axis (a y axis, or a scatter plot's x axis). A value of zero or below becomes a gap, reported
  `non-positive-log-value` once per series with how many.
- `'category'`: one band per category, in order ([`categories`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/categories/)).
- `'time'`: instants on a zone's wall clock ([`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/)). It needs the
  [`timeAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/time-axis/) feature: without it the axis is drawn linear and reported `missing-module`.

Absent, the scale is guessed: category when the data's x values are strings, linear otherwise; time is never guessed.
An unknown scale is reported (`invalid-option`). The keys of another scale are reported (`unknown-option`):
`categories` on a time axis, `zone` on a linear one. The chart's [menu](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/) can offer the user linear or
log, and the view keeps the choice.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('ants')!, {
  title: { text: 'Ants in a made-up colony' },
  xAxis: { title: 'Week' },
  yAxis: { scale: 'log', title: 'Ants' },
  series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'ants', name: 'Ants', data: [[1, 12], [2, 40], [3, 130], [4, 520], [5, 1900], [6, 7400], [7, 26000], [8, 90000]] }],
}, { types: [line] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/): the time axis's clock.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): log scales and time.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/stacking/ -->

# stacking

A y axis's piles drawn as shares of their totals.

Type: `undefined`.

## What it does

`'percent'` on a y axis: at each x, each pile's values become shares of that pile's total, and the axis runs
from 0 to 100 %. An x whose pile totals zero draws nothing there. The series pile up with their `stack` option
([column](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/column/), [bar](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/bar/), [area](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series-types/area/)); the tooltip
and the data table give the share and the value.

Reported (`invalid-option` at `yAxis[0].stacking`) and left out: on an x axis, on a log axis (a pile's parts do not
add up along it), or on a y axis that carries no stacked series. A comparison is not made on a stacked axis.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('harvest')!, {
  title: { text: 'Harvest by plot, as shares (made up)' },
  xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['June', 'July', 'August', 'September'] },
  yAxis: { stacking: 'percent' },
  series: [
    { type: 'column', id: 'beans', name: 'Beans', stack: true, data: [40, 85, 120, 60] },
    { type: 'column', id: 'peas', name: 'Peas', stack: true, data: [70, 55, 20, 10] },
    { type: 'column', id: 'squash', name: 'Squash', stack: true, data: [0, 30, 95, 140] },
  ],
}, { types: [column] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/): another way to read change.
- [Series types](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/series-types/): stacks.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/ticks/ -->

# ticks

How many ticks, how they are written, and their gridlines.

Type: `undefined`.

## What it does

- `target`: about how many ticks to aim for, 2 or more (rounded). The axis still picks round steps (1, 2, 2.5 or 5
  times a power of ten; round units of time) near it. Without it, about one tick every 64 px upright and every 100 px
  across. Labels that would overlap first make fewer ticks; a `target` given is kept.
- `format(value, context)`: the label of a tick, as a string. `value` is the scale's own kind: a number, an instant in
  milliseconds on a time axis, the category's name. `context` gives the chart's `locale` and the `step` between two
  ticks, to choose a precision. A formatter that throws or returns something else than a string: the default label,
  and one `callback-failed` problem at its path (`yAxis[0].ticks.format`).
- `grid`: gridlines across the plot from each tick. On by default for value axes, off for the x axis. Only the first
  value axis draws them; a second one's ticks fall on them.

Without `format`, numbers follow the locale, with the same decimals on every label of an axis, and are shortened past
10 000 (`12K`); a time axis writes only what changes at its unit.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('harvest')!, {
  xAxis: { scale: 'linear', ticks: { grid: true } },
  yAxis: { scale: 'linear', ticks: { target: 4, format: (v, { locale }) => `${new Intl.NumberFormat(locale).format(v)} kg` } },
  series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'harvest', name: 'Harvest', data: [[1, 120], [2, 180], [3, 260], [4, 310], [5, 280]] }],
}, { types: [line] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`min`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/min/) and [`max`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/max/): bounds the ticks fall inside.
- [`locale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/locale/): the language of numbers and dates.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/title/ -->

# title

The axis's name, written beside it.

Type: `undefined`.

## What it does

The title sits beyond the axis's labels: under an x axis, beside a y axis turned to read upwards. Its room is
taken from the plot. With two value axes in use, each title also shows the signs of the series drawn against it, so
a reader knows which line reads on which axis without colour.

Say the unit there (`'Rain (mm)'`): the ticks then stay plain numbers. A title that is not a string is reported
(`invalid-option`) and left out.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('rain')!, {
  xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'] },
  yAxis: [{ id: 'rain', title: 'Rain (mm)' }, { id: 'heat', title: 'Warmth (°C)', opposite: true }],
  series: [
    { type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain', yAxis: 'rain', data: [62, 48, 51, 44, 57, 39] },
    { type: 'line', id: 'heat', name: 'Warmth', yAxis: 'heat', data: [4, 6, 9, 13, 17, 21] },
  ],
}, { types: [column, line] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`opposite`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/opposite/): the far side.
- [`title`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/title/), the chart's own.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/ -->

# zone

The time zone a time axis reads its instants in.

Type: `undefined`. Default: the page’s zone.

## What it does

An IANA name (`'Europe/Paris'`, `'UTC'`). Ticks, labels, the tooltip and the data table read the wall clock of
that zone: a day tick sits at local midnight, even on a day of 23 or 25 hours; an hour the clock repeats gets two
ticks, an hour it skips none. Aggregation periods follow the zone's calendar.

The data's x values are instants: milliseconds since 1970 UTC, or ISO date-times **with** an offset (`…Z`,
`…+01:00`). A calendar day (`'2026-03-29'`) stands at its midnight in this zone. A date-time without an offset is never
guessed: the point is a gap, reported `ambiguous-instant` with how many. An unknown zone name is reported
(`invalid-option`) and the page's zone is used.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(document.getElementById('tide')!, {
  xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'Europe/Paris' },
  series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'tide', name: 'Tide (m)', data: [['2026-03-29T00:00:00Z', 1.2], ['2026-03-29T03:00:00+01:00', 3.8], ['2026-03-29', 2.1]] }],
}, { types: [line], features: [timeAxis] });
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`scale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/): the time scale needs the `timeAxis` feature.
- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): time.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/animate/ -->

# animate

Drive the chart's animations yourself.

Type: `(animation: AnimateHook) => void`.

## What it does

A chart animates its first drawing (400 ms) and each update (250 ms) with its own timing. `animate` takes the
timing over, to follow an app's own motion or a library such as GSAP. It is called instead, with an `AnimateHook`:

- `from` and `to`: the two scenes;
- `duration`: the milliseconds the chart would take;
- `draw(t)`: draws the state at `t`, from 0 (`from`) to 1 (`to`), with any easing the app likes;
- `done()`: ends the animation, drawing the end state if it was not.

A newer animation, or the chart destroyed, makes the older hook's `draw` do nothing. The hook is not called when there
is nothing to animate: under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, or with [`animation: false`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/animation/),
the end state is drawn at once.

`<dz-chart>` takes it as its `[animate]` input; a new value draws a new chart.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, type AnimateHook } from '@dzgraph/dom';

/** Twice as slow as the chart's own timing, at an even pace. */
const slow = (a: AnimateHook) => {
  const start = performance.now();
  const step = (now: number) => {
    const t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / (a.duration * 2));
    a.draw(t);
    if (t < 1) requestAnimationFrame(step);
    else a.done();
  };
  requestAnimationFrame(step);
};

chart(document.getElementById('bees')!, { title: { text: 'Bees seen (made up)' }, series: [{ type: 'column', name: 'Bees', data: [12, 30, 52, 61] }] }, { types: [column], animate: slow });
```

## See also

- [`animation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/animation/): on or off.
- [Interactions](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/interactions/): animation.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/features/ -->

# features

The features a chart may use.

Type: `readonly Feature[]`. Default: `[]`.

## What it does

Each feature is its own import from `@dzgraph/dom`: [`timeAxis`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/time-axis/), [`zoom`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/zoom/), [`navigatorStrip`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/navigator-strip/), [`canvas`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/canvas/), [`webgl`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/webgl/), [`crosshair`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/crosshair/), [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/compare/), [`measure`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/measure/), [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/selection/), [`aggregation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/), [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/drilldown/), [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/menu/), [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/exporting/). A chart does only what its features
allow, and a page ships only the features it imports; `allFeatures` gives every one. Some bring another with them:
`navigatorStrip` brings `zoom`, `webgl` brings `canvas`, `drilldown` brings `aggregation`.

An option that needs a feature the chart was not given is not an error: the chart draws without it and reports
`missing-module`, the feature's name in the problem's detail (a time axis is then drawn linear). Without `canvas`,
every series is drawn in SVG, however many points it has.

`<dz-chart>` takes them as its `[features]` input, or once for the whole app with `provideDzGraph({ types, features })` (`@dzgraph/angular`) in `bootstrapApplication` or a route; a binding on the tag wins. The component imports none itself, so the app ships only those it names; `provideDzGraph({ types: allTypes, features: allFeatures })` gives everything. Neither: no feature.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, navigatorStrip, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('sensor')!,
  {
    title: { text: 'A made-up sensor, one reading a minute' },
    navigator: true,
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC' },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'sensor', name: 'Reading', data: [[1767225600000, 101], [1767225660000, 99.6], [1767225720000, 100.4]] }],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [timeAxis, navigatorStrip] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`types`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/types/): what the chart may draw.
- [Getting started](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/getting-started/typescript/#series-types-and-features): series types and features.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/messages/ -->

# messages

Words to use instead of the built-in ones.

Type: `MessageOverrides`. Default: the built-in words of the page’s language (English or French).

## What it does

A chart writes words of its own: « No data », a series without a name, the summary and each point's label for
screen readers, the tooltip's total, the menu, the breadcrumb, the selection's count. English and French are built in.
The chart picks them by the language of its [`locale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/locale/), else of the nearest `lang` attribute
around it, else of the browser; any other language gets the English words.

`messages` puts the app's words on top, for any language: some words to change, or every word of a language DzGraph
does not ship. Its type is `MessageOverrides` (from `@dzgraph/dom`): any word alone, at any depth. A group of words
(`menu`, `exporting`, `drill`, `shapes`) is merged word by word: `{ drill: { retry: 'Again' } }` changes that word
and keeps the group's others. A word that depends on a value is a function (`seriesName: (place) => …`), replaced
whole. A key the chart has no word for is ignored.

`<dz-chart>` takes them as its `[messages]` input, or once for the whole app with `provideDzGraph({ messages })`; a new
value draws a new chart.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, type MessageOverrides } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const words: MessageOverrides = {
  noData: 'Nothing measured yet',
  seriesName: (place) => `Sensor ${place}`,
};

chart(document.getElementById('sensors')!, { title: { text: 'Garden sensors (made up)' }, series: [{ type: 'line', data: [] }] }, { types: [line], messages: words });
```

## See also

- [`locale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/locale/): the language of numbers, dates and words.
- [Theming and right to left](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/theming-rtl/): the chart's words.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/types/ -->

# types

The series types a chart may draw.

Type: `readonly SeriesType[]`. Required.

## What it does

Each series type is its own import from `@dzgraph/core` (`line`, `area`, `column`, `bar`, `scatter`, `pie`,
`donut`, `gauge`), so a page ships only the types it draws. `allTypes` gives every one, for an app that does not count
bytes. A series of a type the chart was not given is left out and reported `unknown-series-type` at its `type`, with
the type's name.

`<dz-chart>` takes them as its `[types]` input, or once for the whole app with `provideDzGraph({ types, features })` (`@dzgraph/angular`) in `bootstrapApplication` or a route; a binding on the tag wins. The component imports none itself, so the app ships only those it names; `provideDzGraph({ types: allTypes, features: allFeatures })` gives everything. Neither: no type, and each series is reported.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('jars')!,
  {
    title: { text: 'Jars sold (made up)' },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'jars', name: 'Jars', data: [42, 38, 51, 47] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'target', name: 'Target', data: [45, 45, 50, 50] },
      { type: 'pie', id: 'shares', name: 'Shares', data: [3, 2, 1] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column, line] },
);
for (const p of c.problems) console.warn(p.code, p.path); // unknown-series-type series[2].type
```

## See also

- [`features`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/setup/features/): what the chart may do.
- [Getting started](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/getting-started/typescript/#series-types-and-features): series types and features.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/ -->

# aggregation

Points grouped by period of the calendar or by bucket of x.

Import: `aggregation` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

It lets the x axis's [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/) work, and lets the [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/menu/) offer
« Aggregation ». Each series is drawn as one point per period (`'hour'` to `'year'`, on the axis's zone's calendar; a
week starts on Monday) or per bucket of a numeric x (`{ step }`). Its value is the series' function of the points in it,
set by the series' [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/aggregate/): a sum for columns and bars, a mean otherwise. A period
without points is a gap, not a zero.

The axis keeps its own ticks and each point stands at its period's start. The tooltip's heading names the period and
says how many points it holds; the data table lists the groups. Selecting a group selects every point it holds.
Stacked series aggregate before they stack. A category axis or a pie has nothing to aggregate (`invalid-option`). The
user's choice from the menu is part of the view. [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/drilldown/) brings it for `drilldown: 'time'`.

Without it, `aggregate` is reported (`missing-module`).

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { aggregation, chart, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('rain')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'Europe/Paris', aggregate: 'week' },
    series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'rain', name: 'Rain (mm)', data: [['2026-03-02', 4], ['2026-03-04', 9], ['2026-03-10', 2], ['2026-03-12', 7], ['2026-03-18', 12]] }],
  },
  { types: [column], features: [timeAxis, aggregation] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/aggregate/), the axis option.
- [`aggregate`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/aggregate/), the series option.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/canvas/ -->

# canvas

A Canvas plane for series of many marks.

Import: `canvas` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

There is no option: given the feature, a series that draws more than 2 000 marks (markers, columns) is painted
on a Canvas, under the axes and the labels. It looks the same as in SVG: the same colours read from the theme, the
same sizes, aligned to the pixel. Hovering, the focus ring and the tooltip do not change. A series of fewer marks
stays in SVG, and so do lines and areas of any length: they are thinned to what the plot can show (decimated) and stay
crisp.

Without it, every series is drawn in SVG: the same picture, with an element per mark. The PNG export draws the
Canvas marks too; the SVG export writes each mark as an element, but only those that can show in the plot.
[`webgl`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/webgl/) goes further for scatters past 100 000 points, and falls back on this Canvas when WebGL2 is not
there.

## Example

```ts
import { scatter } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { canvas, chart } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const n = 20_000;
const x = new Float64Array(n);
const y = new Float64Array(n);
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  x[i] = (i * 7919) % 1000;
  y[i] = (i * 104_729) % 1000;
}
chart(
  document.getElementById('dots')!,
  { series: [{ type: 'scatter', id: 'dots', name: 'Dots', data: { x, y } }] },
  { types: [scatter], features: [canvas] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Big data](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/big-data/): the guide, with the measured costs.
- [`webgl`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/webgl/), for the densest scatters.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/compare/ -->

# compare

Series shown against a baseline: as a difference, in percent, or as base 100.

Import: `compare` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

It lets a y axis's [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/) draw, and lets the [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/menu/) offer
« Comparison ». Each series on that axis is drawn against its baseline: `'value'` as the difference, `'percent'` as the
change in percent, `'index'` as base 100. The baseline is each series' first point with a value in view, so zooming
or panning moves it; [`compareTo`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare-to/) fixes it at an x.

The axis writes signed values (« +10 », « +12 % »), and a line marks the reference. The tooltip gives the compared value
first, then the raw one; the data table gives both. A series with no baseline in view (or a base of 0 in percent and
base 100) is not drawn, and a `no-baseline` problem says so until the range gives it one. Stacked series and log axes
are not compared (`invalid-option`). The user's choice is part of the view.

Without it, `compare` is reported (`missing-module`).

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, compare } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('shops')!,
  {
    yAxis: { compare: 'percent' },
    series: [
      { type: 'line', id: 'north', name: 'North shop', data: [120, 132, 128, 150, 161] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'south', name: 'South shop', data: [80, 78, 90, 99, 97] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [compare] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare/), the axis option.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/crosshair/ -->

# crosshair

Lines through the pointer, with its values on the axes.

Import: `crosshair` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

It lets the [`crosshair`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/crosshair/) option draw: a dashed vertical line that follows the pointer
exactly, with a tag at its foot giving the x value there, and with `{ horizontal: true }` a horizontal line and a tag on
each value axis. The tags are kept inside the chart's edges. With the keyboard the lines go through the focused point;
on touch they follow the finger while it is down. Leaving the plot removes them. They stay in the measure and selection
modes, to help aim. Screen readers hear nothing more: the values are the focused point's, already said.

Linked charts can share it ([`linkCharts()`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/)), and `showX()` draws it at an x value from the
app. Not on a pie, a donut or a gauge.

Without it, `crosshair` is reported (`missing-module`) and nothing is drawn.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, crosshair } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('bees')!,
  { crosshair: true, series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'bees', name: 'Bees', data: [12, 30, 52, 61, 58, 44, 23] }] },
  { types: [column], features: [crosshair] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`crosshair`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/crosshair/), the option.
- [Interactions](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/interactions/): the guide.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/drilldown/ -->

# drilldown

A point's detail by click or Enter, with a breadcrumb to go back.

Import: `drilldown` from `@dzgraph/dom`. Brings `aggregation`.

## What it does

It lets two options work: a series' [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/drilldown/), which gives each point's detail by
its key (`details`) or loads it (`load`), and the chart's [`drilldown: 'time'`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/drilldown/), which drills a
time axis from years into months, and from a month into days.

A click or Enter on a point that has a detail shows the detail in its place, animated. A breadcrumb above the plot names
each level; each but the last is a link back. Backspace, and Alt + ← (→ in right to left), go up one level, and going
up restores the level as it was: its range, its hidden series, its selection. A load shows « Loading… »; one that fails
or takes more than 10 s says so and offers « Try again ».

The level is part of the view: `getView()` gives the path of keys from the root, `setView()` goes there, and the `drill`
event gives the path. Linked charts share the level.

Without it, both options are reported (`missing-module`) and a click does nothing more.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, drilldown } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('fruit')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'category', categories: ['Apples', 'Pears'] },
    series: [{
      type: 'column',
      id: 'fruit',
      name: 'Fruit picked',
      data: { y: [52, 31], key: ['apples', 'pears'] },
      drilldown: { details: { apples: [{ type: 'column', id: 'apples', name: 'Varieties', data: [['Gala', 30], ['Reinette', 22]] }] } },
    }],
  },
  { types: [column], features: [drilldown] },
);
c.on('drill', (e) => console.log(e.path));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/series/drilldown/), the series option.
- [`drilldown`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/drilldown/), the chart option.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/exporting/ -->

# exporting

Export and printing: SVG, PNG and CSV, a download, print.

Import: `exporting` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

It gives the chart's export methods their work, and the [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/menu/) its « Download » and « Print »
entries:

| Method | What it gives |
|---|---|
| `exportSvg(options?)` | the view as a standalone SVG document (a string) |
| `exportPng(options?)` | the view as a PNG (a promise of a `Blob`) |
| `exportCsv(options?)` | the data as CSV (a string), the rows the table shows |
| `download(format, options?)` | the browser's save of `'png'`, `'svg'` or `'csv'`, named after the title |
| `print(options?)` | the chart alone, printed in light colours; `table: true` adds its data table |

A picture is the view as on screen (the visible range, hidden series left out, the selection, the comparison) with the
title, the axes and the legend, but without the controls, the tooltip or the focus ring. Its colours are the screen's
unless `theme` asks for `'light'` or `'dark'`; `width` and `height` lay the chart out again at that size; a PNG is
drawn at `scale` device pixels per CSS pixel, at least 2 by default. The SVG carries its colours and fonts, a title and
a description. The CSV writes raw values, times in ISO 8601 with their offset, and guards cells against formulas;
`locale: true` uses the language's separators. The [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/exporting/) option sets the defaults.

Without it, the methods give `null` or do nothing, and report `missing-module`.

## Example

```ts
import { column } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, exporting } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('crates')!,
  { title: { text: 'Crates picked (made up)' }, series: [{ type: 'column', id: 'crates', name: 'Crates', data: [12, 19, 15, 22, 17] }] },
  { types: [column], features: [exporting] },
);
document.getElementById('save')!.addEventListener('click', () => void c.download('png', { theme: 'light' }));
const csv = c.exportCsv();
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/exporting/), the option.
- [Export and print](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exporting/): the guide.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/measure/ -->

# measure

Measuring between two points: the Measure mode, and M on a focused point.

Import: `measure` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

There is no option: given the feature, the chart has a « Measure » mode. With [`zoom`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/zoom/) or
[`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/selection/) too, a mode bar at the start of the plot's top edge chooses what a drag does; alone, a drag
measures. `setMode('measure')` sets the mode from the app, and `modeChange` tells it.

In measure mode, pressing on the plot picks the nearest point; dragging, the end snaps to the nearest point; releasing
keeps the measure. A line joins the two points, and a tag at its middle gives the difference in value, in percent of
the start, and along x (a duration on a time axis, a count on a category axis). Two series may be measured. Escape, a
click outside it, a new measure, a change of mode or new data remove it; a zoom keeps it on its points.

With the keyboard, on a focused point, M starts a measure there in any mode; moving the focus moves its end; M again
keeps it, and screen readers hear it. The `measure` event gives the two points, and `null` when it goes. A measure is
not part of the view.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, measure, zoom } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('plant')!,
  { series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'plant', name: 'Height (cm)', data: [3, 5, 8, 12, 17, 21, 24] }] },
  { types: [line], features: [zoom, measure] },
);
c.setMode('measure');
c.on('measure', (m) => console.log(m ? [m.from.index, m.to.index] : null));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.
- [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/selection/), the other mode.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/menu/ -->

# menu

The chart menu: a series' type, the aggregation, the scale, the comparison, export and print.

Import: `menu` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

It lets the [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/) option draw: a small « Chart options » button at the end of the chart's
top edge, which opens a menu of the items the app lists (`true`: all of them) and that make sense for the data.

- **Type**: a series' type among those that suit its data (line, area, column).
- **Aggregation**: none, or a period with its function, on a time axis (with [`aggregation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/)).
- **Scale**: linear or logarithmic for the value axis; logarithmic only when every value is positive.
- **Comparison**: none, difference, percent, base 100 (with [`compare`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/compare/)).
- **Download** (PNG, SVG, CSV) and **Print**, with [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/exporting/).

It follows the menu button pattern: Enter, Space or ↓ open it on its first item; the arrows move; Enter or Space choose;
Escape closes it and gives the focus back; → and ← open and close a submenu. A choice applies at once, animated, and is
part of the view. A menu with nothing to offer shows no button.

Without it, `menu` is reported (`missing-module`) and no button is shown.

## Example

```ts
import { column, line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, menu } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('jars')!,
  {
    menu: { items: ['type', 'scale'] },
    series: [
      { type: 'column', id: 'honey', name: 'Honey', data: [14, 22, 19, 27] },
      { type: 'line', id: 'jam', name: 'Jam', data: [9, 12, 16, 15] },
    ],
  },
  { types: [column, line], features: [menu] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`menu`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/menu/), the option.
- [`exporting`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/exporting/), for Download and Print.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/navigator-strip/ -->

# navigatorStrip

The navigator strip under the plot, and the range buttons above it.

Import: `navigatorStrip` from `@dzgraph/dom`. Brings `zoom`.

## What it does

It lets two options draw: [`navigator`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/navigator/) and
[`rangeButtons`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/range-buttons/). It is not named `navigator`: that name would hide the browser's global
of the same name in your module.

- **The navigator**: a strip under the plot draws the visible series over their whole x range, thin, with its own
  light labels. A window marks the visible range, the rest is shaded, and a handle sits on each edge. Dragging the
  window moves the range, dragging a handle moves that end, and a click outside the window moves it there. With the
  keyboard the handles are sliders (« Start of range », « End of range »): the arrows move them by a hundredth of the
  whole, Page Up and Page Down by a tenth. The chart and the strip follow each other.
- **The range buttons**, on a time axis: « 1m », « 3m », « YTD », « 1y », « All », above the plot at the start of the
  reading direction. Each shows a span ending at the last point, on the axis's calendar; a span longer than the data is
  disabled, and the button matching the range is pressed.

Without it, `navigator` and `rangeButtons` are reported (`missing-module`) and nothing is drawn.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, navigatorStrip, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const days = Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, i) => [Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1) + i * 86_400_000, 50 + (i % 30)] as [number, number]);
chart(
  document.getElementById('visits')!,
  { navigator: true, rangeButtons: true, xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'UTC' }, series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'visits', name: 'Visitors', data: days }] },
  { types: [line], features: [timeAxis, navigatorStrip] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`navigator`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/navigator/), the option.
- [`rangeButtons`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/range-buttons/), the option.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/selection/ -->

# selection

Selecting points: a rectangle, a range of x or a lasso; Space on a focused point.

Import: `selection` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

It lets the [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/selection/) option work. A drag selects with the current shape: by
default a range of x on lines and areas, a rectangle on scatters and columns; `shapes` lists those offered, and with
more than one the mode's button opens a choice. The lasso is exact, live while drawing, even at a million points. With
[`zoom`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/zoom/) or [`measure`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/measure/) too, a mode bar chooses what a drag does.

- A drag replaces the selection; with Shift it adds, with Alt it removes.
- A click on a point selects it alone, Shift + click adds or removes it; a click on empty plot or Escape clears.
- On a focused point, Space selects or unselects it, and Shift + ← → extends the selection along its series.
- A pie or a donut selects by click, Shift + click and Space, with no mode bar.

Selected points keep their colour and the others fade; a column, bar or slice gets a ring too, so colour is not the
only sign. Screen readers hear how many points are selected, and the data table marks their rows. The selection is
data, not pixels: it survives zoom, resize and hidden series. `selectionChange` gives the count and each series'
indices and keys; `selectBy()` selects from the app; the view keeps it.

Without it, `selection` is reported (`missing-module`).

## Example

```ts
import { scatter } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, selection } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('leaves')!,
  {
    selection: { shapes: ['rectangle', 'lasso'] },
    series: [{ type: 'scatter', id: 'leaves', name: 'Leaves', data: [[4.1, 2.2], [5.3, 2.9], [6.0, 3.4], [7.2, 3.1], [3.8, 1.9]] }],
  },
  { types: [scatter], features: [selection] },
);
c.on('selectionChange', (e) => console.log(e.count));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/chart/selection/), the option.
- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/time-axis/ -->

# timeAxis

Time scales: instants and days in a zone, ticks on the calendar.

Import: `timeAxis` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

With it, an axis takes `scale: 'time'` (see [`scale`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/scale/)). It reads instants: numbers
(milliseconds since 1970 UTC) or ISO date-times with an offset (`2026-03-29T01:30:00+01:00`, `…Z`). A date-time
without an offset is never guessed: the point is a gap, reported `ambiguous-instant`. A calendar day (`2026-03-29`)
stands at its local midnight in the axis's [`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/), the page's zone by default.

Ticks fall on round values of the zone's wall clock: years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds. A label says only
what changes at its unit (« 2026 », « Mar », « 3 », « 14:00 »), and under days or hours a second row names the month
or the date where it changes. A day tick stays at local midnight on a day of 23 or 25 hours. The tooltip's heading and
the data table give the full date and time in the zone.

It also reads the time values of [`setRange()`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/), [`compareTo`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/compare-to/) and
the axis's `min` and `max`, and it is what [`aggregation`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/aggregation/) groups by calendar period.

Without it, `scale: 'time'` is reported (`missing-module`) and the axis is drawn as a linear one.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, timeAxis } from '@dzgraph/dom';

chart(
  document.getElementById('visits')!,
  {
    xAxis: { scale: 'time', zone: 'Europe/Paris' },
    series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'visits', name: 'Visitors', data: [['2026-03-27', 41], ['2026-03-28', 58], ['2026-03-29', 52], ['2026-03-30', 66]] }],
  },
  { types: [line], features: [timeAxis] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Axes and time](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/axes-time/): the guide.
- [`zone`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/axis/zone/), the axis's zone.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/webgl/ -->

# webgl

WebGL2 for scatters past 100 000 points.

Import: `webgl` from `@dzgraph/dom`. Brings `canvas`.

## What it does

There is no option: given the feature, a scatter of more than 100 000 points (the threshold the benches set)
is drawn by WebGL2. It looks the same as on Canvas: the same colours from the theme, the same symbols and sizes, the
same translucency (piles read darker), on the device-pixel grid, under the axes and the labels. Zooming and panning
cost almost no script: the points stay on the graphics card, and a frame only changes where they go, exact to the
pixel however deep the zoom. Hovering still finds the nearest point within 24 px.

A chart opens a WebGL context only when it first draws such a scatter, and frees it at once when destroyed: a browser
allows only about sixteen per page. Without WebGL2 (an old browser, too many contexts, the graphics card lost), the
same picture is drawn on [`canvas`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/canvas/), without a word to the user; WebGL2 draws again when the card comes
back.

Without the feature, such a scatter is drawn on Canvas, or in SVG without `canvas` either.

## Example

```ts
import { scatter } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, webgl, zoom } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const n = 500_000;
const x = new Float64Array(n);
const y = new Float64Array(n);
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  x[i] = (i * 7919) % 10_000;
  y[i] = (i * 104_729) % 10_000;
}
chart(
  document.getElementById('dots')!,
  { series: [{ type: 'scatter', id: 'dots', name: 'Dots', data: { x, y } }] },
  { types: [scatter], features: [webgl, zoom] },
);
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Big data](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/big-data/): the guide, with the measured costs.
- [`canvas`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/canvas/), which it brings.

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/zoom/ -->

# zoom

Zoom and pan by the user: drag, Shift + drag, Ctrl/⌘ + wheel, pinch, keys.

Import: `zoom` from `@dzgraph/dom`.

## What it does

There is no option: given the feature, the user can zoom the x axis.

- **Mouse or pen**: a drag across the plot draws a band over the x range it covers, and releasing zooms to it (a drag
  shorter than 5 px is a click). Once zoomed, Shift + drag moves the range.
- **Wheel**: the wheel scrolls the page, as on any page; Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) + wheel zooms around the pointer.
- **Touch**: pinching zooms around the fingers' middle; once zoomed, a one-finger slide moves the range.
- **Keyboard**, on a focused point: + and − zoom around it, Shift + ← and → move the range, 0 shows everything.

Zoomed, a « Reset zoom » button appears at the end of the plot's top edge. A zoom never goes past the data's ends, nor
closer than two points across the plot; on a category axis it covers whole categories. The value axes fit the points
in view, unless their bounds are fixed.

The range is part of the view: `rangeChange` gives its bounds (`null` for the whole), `getView()` keeps it and
`setView()` gives it back. With [`selection`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/selection/) or [`measure`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/measure/), a mode bar chooses what a
drag does; Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms in every mode.

## Example

```ts
import { line } from '@dzgraph/core';
import { chart, zoom } from '@dzgraph/dom';

const c = chart(
  document.getElementById('sales')!,
  { series: [{ type: 'line', id: 'sales', name: 'Sales', data: [12, 18, 15, 22, 30, 27, 35, 31, 40, 38] }] },
  { types: [line], features: [zoom] },
);
c.on('rangeChange', (e) => console.log(e.range));
```

## Live demo

## See also

- [Exploring](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/guides/exploring/): the guide.
- [`navigatorStrip`](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgraph/options/features/navigator-strip/): the navigator and the range buttons.
